text:
Abstract
We queried NCBI GEO for Escherichia coli expression studies mentioning ciprofloxacin. Using the GEO Series (GSE) filter, the search returned 37 total matches, with 20 records retrieved in this page (truncated to the top results). From these 20, 15 were annotated as “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing” (including one SuperSeries with expression and other assays), 11 explicitly referenced ciprofloxacin exposure or resistance in the title or summary, and 17 carried a registered PubMed link. These studies span diverse experimental contexts: acute ciprofloxacin exposure time courses, tolerance/resistance mechanisms (e.g., purA, ptsI), multi-antibiotic comparisons including ciprofloxacin, and systems-level responses. Processed expression matrices are available only via each Series’ FTP directory. The result establishes that E. coli ciprofloxacin-related expression data exist in GEO in multiple, recent studies, with sufficient metadata to support downstream reanalysis. Identifying these records and their download locations matters for antibiotic-response research, enabling comparative transcriptomic analyses of fluoroquinolone stress, tolerance, and resistance across experimental designs. Future work can resolve a subset for detailed reanalysis and fetch per-study files via their FTP links.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli is a Gram-negative bacterium and a major model organism in microbiology. Ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, targets DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV and elicits DNA damage responses and stress physiology. Expression studies measuring transcriptomic changes under ciprofloxacin can illuminate tolerance and resistance mechanisms.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. The availability and scope of E. coli expression studies related to ciprofloxacin in public repositories had not been enumerated for this query.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine whether GEO contains E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin and quantify the returned set. Hypothesis: GEO holds multiple GSE entries in which E. coli transcriptomes were measured under ciprofloxacin exposure or in ciprofloxacin resistance contexts.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted NCBI GEO because it indexes processed gene expression studies and supports organism and free-text filtering. We used the Series (GSE) entry type to focus on reusable study units.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO via functions.geo_search
Procedures.
- functions.geo_search with arguments:
  - organism="Escherichia coli"
  - term="ciprofloxacin"
  - entry_type="gse"
  - max_results
